cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Be Right in Retrospect
cards.instruction: Perform certainty by reinterpreting every surprise as something your earlier words were obviously predicting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll sort the refund. I said this holiday would have a sunny ending, and a cheque will brighten things up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You said sunny weather. We spent a week indoors.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which is why we're getting the money back. Give me the receipts; I'll make the call.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You booked it. You explain why we packed sunglasses for a flood.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll explain everything. Keep the sunglasses handy; you'll need them for the smile when I get our money back.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 leads refund and reinterprets sunny forecast; A3 requests receipts; A5 accepts explanation but its sunglasses-smile image does not plausibly ask B for anything needed.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 rainy failure causes A3 refund claim; B4 booking responsibility causes A5 assurance, then an unrelated optical metaphor.

relationship.evidence: B4 legitimately insists the person who booked explain the mismatch.

heightening.evidence: A5 returns to sunglasses but a smile requiring them is a detached exaggeration rather than an earned practical development.

specificity.evidence: A1 refund and B2 rain legible; B4 flood raises severity explicitly, but A5 bright smile creates an unnecessary figurative layer.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 smile-and-sunglasses phrase is authorial wit instead of believable recovery talk.
